sanskrit: evam astv iti taṃ vahniḥ pratyuvāca pitāmaham jagāma śāsanaṃ kartuṃ devasya parameṣṭhinaḥ
english: "So be it," replied Fire to the grandsire Brahmā, and went forth to carry out the command of the supreme lord.

sanskrit: devarṣayaś ca muditās tato jagmur yathāgatam ṛṣayaś ca yathāpūrvaṃ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ pracakrire
english: The divine sages departed joyfully as they had come, and the rishis resumed all their rites as before.

sanskrit: divi devā mumudire bhūtasaṃghāś ca laukikāḥ agniś ca paramāṃ prītim avāpa hatakalmaṣaḥ
english: The gods in heaven rejoiced, as did all the assemblies of living beings on earth, and Fire, his taint removed, attained the highest delight.

sanskrit: evam eṣa purāvṛtta itihāso 'gniśāpajaḥ pulomasya vināśaś ca cyavanasya ca saṃbhavaḥ
english: Such is this ancient tale born of Fire's curse — the destruction of Pulomā and the birth of Cyavana.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca sa cāpi cyavano brahman bhārgavo 'janayat sutam sukanyāyāṃ mahātmānaṃ pramatiṃ dīptatejasam
english: The Sūta said: That Cyavana of Bhṛgu's line, O brahmin, begot upon Sukanyā a son, the great-souled Pramati of blazing energy.

sanskrit: pramatis tu ruruṃ nāma ghṛtācyāṃ samajījanat ruruḥ pramadvarāyāṃ tu śunakaṃ samajījanat
english: Pramati begot upon Ghṛtācī a son named Ruru; and Ruru begot upon Pramadvara a son named Śunaka.

sanskrit: tasya brahman ruroḥ sarvaṃ caritaṃ bhūritejasaḥ vistareṇa pravakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu tvam aśeṣataḥ
english: Of that Ruru of great splendor, O brahmin, I shall recount the entire story in full — hear it without omission.

sanskrit: ṛṣir āsīn mahān pūrvaṃ tapovidyāsamanvitaḥ sthūlakeśa iti khyātaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: There was in former times a great rishi endowed with austerity and knowledge, known by the name Sthulakesha, devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu menakāyāṃ prajajñivān gandharvarājo viprarṣe viśvāvasur iti śrutaḥ
english: In that very time, O brahmin-rishi, the king of the gandharvas known as Viśvāvasu had fathered a child upon Menakā.

sanskrit: athāpsarā menakā sā taṃ garbhaṃ bhṛgunandana utsasarja yathākālaṃ sthūlakeśāśramaṃ prati
english: Then the apsara Menakā, O son of Bhṛgu's line, abandoned that embryo in due time near the hermitage of Sthulakesha.

sanskrit: utsṛjya caiva taṃ garbhaṃ nadyās tīre jagāma ha kanyām amaragarbhābhāṃ jvalantīm iva ca śriyā
english: Having abandoned the embryo on the riverbank, she departed; the infant girl shone with the beauty of a celestial child, blazing as it were with radiant glory.

sanskrit: tāṃ dadarśa samutsṛṣṭāṃ nadītīre mahān ṛṣiḥ sthūlakeśaḥ sa tejasvī vijane bandhuvarjitām
english: The great rishi Sthulakesha, that splendid one, saw her abandoned on the riverbank, alone, bereft of kin.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā kanyāṃ sthūlakeśo dvijottamaḥ jagrāhātha muniśreṣṭhaḥ kṛpāviṣṭaḥ pupoṣa ca vavṛdhe sā varārohā tasyāśramapade śubhā
english: Seeing that girl, Sthulakesha, best of twice-born men, that foremost sage, filled with compassion, took her in and nurtured her; and she of lovely form grew up beautifully in his hermitage.

sanskrit: pramadābhyo varā sā tu sarvarūpaguṇānvitā tataḥ pramadvarety asyā nāma cakre mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: She was the most excellent among women, endowed with beauty and virtue in every way; and so the great rishi gave her the name Pramadvara.

sanskrit: tām āśramapade tasya rurur dṛṣṭvā pramadvarām babhūva kila dharmātmā madanānugatātmavān
english: Ruru, the righteous-souled one, on seeing Pramadvara at that hermitage, found his heart overtaken by the god of love.

sanskrit: pitaraṃ sakhibhiḥ so 'tha vācayām āsa bhārgavaḥ pramatiś cābhyayāc chrutvā sthūlakeśaṃ yaśasvinam
english: Then that scion of Bhṛgu's line had his friends convey his wish to his father, and Pramati, having heard, went himself to the illustrious Sthulakesha.

sanskrit: tataḥ prādāt pitā kanyāṃ rurave tāṃ pramadvarām vivāhaṃ sthāpayitvāgre nakṣatre bhagadaivate
english: Then the father gave that maiden Pramadvara to Ruru, having first fixed the wedding for the auspicious asterism presided over by Bhaga.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya vivāhe samupasthite sakhībhiḥ krīḍatī sārdhaṃ sā kanyā varavarṇinī
english: Then, a few days before the wedding arrived, that fair-complexioned maiden was playing with her companions,

sanskrit: nāpaśyata prasuptaṃ vai bhujagaṃ tiryag āyatam padā cainaṃ samākrāman mumūrṣuḥ kālacoditā
english: when she did not notice a serpent lying asleep stretched across her path; she stepped upon it, driven by fate toward death.

sanskrit: sa tasyāḥ saṃpramattāyāś coditaḥ kāladharmaṇā viṣopaliptān daśanān bhṛśam aṅge nyapātayat
english: The serpent, urged on by the law of time, drove its venom-smeared fangs deep into her body while she was careless.

sanskrit: sā daṣṭā sahasā bhūmau patitā gatacetanā vyasur aprekṣaṇīyāpi prekṣaṇīyatamākṛtiḥ
english: Bitten, she instantly fell to the ground, her senses gone, her life departed — yet even lifeless her form was supremely beautiful to behold.

sanskrit: prasuptevābhavac cāpi bhuvi sarpaviṣārditā bhūyo manoharatarā babhūva tanumadhyamā
english: She lay upon the earth as if asleep, tormented by the serpent's venom; the slender-waisted one became even more heart-ravishing than before.

sanskrit: dadarśa tāṃ pitā caiva te caivānye tapasvinaḥ viceṣṭamānāṃ patitāṃ bhūtale padmavarcasam
english: Her father and the other ascetics saw her fallen on the ground, her lotus-radiant form convulsed.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve dvijavarāḥ samājagmuḥ kṛpānvitāḥ svastyātreyo mahājānuḥ kuśikaḥ śaṅkhamekhalaḥ
english: Then all the best of twice-born men gathered filled with compassion — Svastyatreya, Mahajanu, Kuśika, Shankhamekhala,

sanskrit: bhāradvājaḥ kauṇakutsa ārṣṭiṣeṇo 'tha gautamaḥ pramatiḥ saha putreṇa tathānye vanavāsinaḥ
english: Bharadvaja, Kaunakutsa, Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, Gautama, Pramati with his son, and other forest-dwellers as well.

sanskrit: tāṃ te kanyāṃ vyasuṃ dṛṣṭvā bhujagasya viṣārditām ruruduḥ kṛpayāviṣṭā rurus tv ārto bahir yayau
english: Seeing that maiden lifeless, afflicted by the serpent's poison, they wept, overcome with compassion; but Ruru, stricken with grief, went away into the forest.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca teṣu tatropaviṣṭeṣu brāhmaṇeṣu samantataḥ ruruś cukrośa gahanaṃ vanaṃ gatvā suduḥkhitaḥ
english: The Sūta said: While the brahmins sat there on all sides, Ruru went into the dense forest and wept aloud, overcome with great sorrow.

sanskrit: śokenābhihataḥ so 'tha vilapan karuṇaṃ bahu abravīd vacanaṃ śocan priyāṃ cintya pramadvarām
english: Struck down by grief, lamenting piteously and at length, he spoke these words in sorrow, thinking of his beloved Pramadvara:

sanskrit: śete sā bhuvi tanvaṅgī mama śokavivardhinī bāndhavānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param
english: "She, the slender-limbed one who multiplies my grief, lies upon the earth — what sorrow greater than this could there be for all her kinsmen?

sanskrit: yadi dattaṃ tapas taptaṃ guravo vā mayā yadi samyag ārādhitās tena saṃjīvatu mama priyā
english: If I have performed austerities, if I have duly honored my teachers — by that merit let my beloved come back to life.

sanskrit: yathā janmaprabhṛti vai yatātmāhaṃ dhṛtavrataḥ pramadvarā tathādyaiva samuttiṣṭhatu bhāminī
english: As I have been self-restrained and steadfast in my vows from birth, so let the fiery Pramadvara rise up this very day."

sanskrit: devadūta uvāca abhidhatse ha yad vācā ruro duḥkhena tan mṛṣā na tu martyasya dharmātmann āyur asti gatāyuṣaḥ
english: A divine messenger said: "Ruru, what you speak in your grief is in vain — there is no life remaining for one whose life has departed, O righteous one.

sanskrit: gatāyur eṣā kṛpaṇā gandharvāpsarasoḥ sutā tasmāc choke manas tāta mā kṛthās tvaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: This pitiable one, daughter of a gandharva and an apsara, has exhausted her lifespan. Therefore, dear son, do not in any way set your mind on grief.

sanskrit: upāyaś cātra vihitaḥ pūrvaṃ devair mahātmabhiḥ taṃ yadīcchasi kartuṃ tvaṃ prāpsyasīmāṃ pramadvarām
english: Yet a means was ordained here long ago by the great-souled gods; if you wish to perform it, you shall recover this Pramadvara."

sanskrit: rurur uvāca ka upāyaḥ kṛto devair brūhi tattvena khecara kariṣye taṃ tathā śrutvā trātum arhati māṃ bhavān
english: Ruru said: "What means did the gods ordain? Tell me truly, O sky-traveler. Having heard it I will perform it accordingly — you must save me."

sanskrit: devadūta uvāca āyuṣo 'rdhaṃ prayacchasva kanyāyai bhṛgunandana evam utthāsyati ruro tava bhāryā pramadvarā
english: The divine messenger said: "Give half of your remaining lifespan to the maiden, O son of Bhṛgu's line — then your wife Pramadvara will rise, O Ruru."

sanskrit: rurur uvāca āyuṣo 'rdhaṃ prayacchāmi kanyāyai khecarottama śṛṅgārarūpābharaṇā uttiṣṭhatu mama priyā
english: Ruru said: "I give half my lifespan to the maiden, O best of sky-travelers. Let my beloved, adorned with the ornaments of love's beauty, rise up."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tato gandharvarājaś ca devadūtaś ca sattamau dharmarājam upetyedaṃ vacanaṃ pratyabhāṣatām
english: The Sūta said: Then both the king of the gandharvas and the divine messenger, those most excellent ones, went to Dharmarāja and spoke these words:

sanskrit: dharmarājāyuṣo 'rdhena ruror bhāryā pramadvarā samuttiṣṭhatu kalyāṇī mṛtaiva yadi manyase
english: "Let the auspicious Pramadvara, wife of Ruru, rise up in exchange for half of Ruru's lifespan — if you see fit, O Dharmarāja, even though she is dead."

sanskrit: dharmarāja uvāca pramadvarā ruror bhāryā devadūta yadīcchasi uttiṣṭhatv āyuṣo 'rdhena ruror eva samanvitā
english: Dharmarāja said: "O divine messenger, if you wish it, let Pramadvara, Ruru's wife, rise up endowed with half of Ruru's own lifespan."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam ukte tataḥ kanyā sodatiṣṭhat pramadvarā ruros tasyāyuṣo 'rdhena supteva varavarṇinī
english: The Sūta said: When this was spoken, then the maiden Pramadvara rose up, endowed with half of Ruru's lifespan, as if waking from sleep, that fair-complexioned one.

sanskrit: etad dṛṣṭaṃ bhaviṣye hi ruror uttamatejasaḥ āyuṣo 'tipravṛddhasya bhāryārthe 'rdhaṃ hrasatv iti
english: "This has been witnessed: for Ruru of supreme splendor, whose lifespan is greatly extended, let it be diminished by half for the sake of his wife" — so it was decreed.

sanskrit: tata iṣṭe 'hani tayoḥ pitarau cakratur mudā vivāhaṃ tau ca remāte parasparahitaiṣiṇau
english: Then on an auspicious day their two fathers joyfully performed the wedding, and those two who wished each other's good rejoiced together.

sanskrit: sa labdhvā durlabhāṃ bhāryāṃ padmakiñjalkasaprabhām vrataṃ cakre vināśāya jihmagānāṃ dhṛtavrataḥ
english: Having obtained his priceless wife who shone like lotus filaments, he of firm resolve made a vow to destroy all serpents.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā jihmagān sarvāṃs tīvrakopasamanvitaḥ abhihanti yathāsannaṃ gṛhya praharaṇaṃ sadā
english: He, filled with fierce rage, whenever he saw any serpent, would always seize a weapon and strike it down, however near it was.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid vanaṃ vipro rurur abhyāgaman mahat śayānaṃ tatra cāpaśyaḍ ḍuṇḍubhaṃ vayasānvitam
english: One day the brahmin Ruru came to a great forest, and there he saw an aged dundubha serpent lying asleep.

sanskrit: tata udyamya daṇḍaṃ sa kāladaṇḍopamaṃ tadā abhyaghnad ruṣito vipras tam uvācātha ḍuṇḍubhaḥ
english: Then the brahmin, filled with rage, raised his staff resembling the staff of death and struck at it; but the dundubha spoke:

sanskrit: nāparādhyāmi te kiṃ cid aham adya tapodhana saṃrambhāt tat kimarthaṃ mām abhihaṃsi ruṣānvitaḥ
english: "I have done you no wrong at all today, O ascetic. Why then do you attack me in this rage, filled with fury?"

sanskrit: rurur uvāca mama prāṇasamā bhāryā daṣṭāsīd bhujagena ha tatra me samayo ghora ātmanoraga vai kṛtaḥ
english: Ruru said: "My wife, who is as dear to me as my own life, was bitten by a serpent; and because of that I have made a terrible vow regarding serpents:

sanskrit: hanyāṃ sadaiva bhujagaṃ yaṃ yaṃ paśyeyam ity uta tato 'haṃ tvāṃ jighāṃsāmi jīvitena vimokṣyase
english: "I will always slay whatever serpent I see." Therefore I intend to kill you — save yourself with your life if you can.

sanskrit: ḍuṇḍubha uvāca anye te bhujagā vipra ye daśantīha mānavān ḍuṇḍubhān ahigandhena na tvaṃ hiṃsitum arhasi
english: The dundubha said: "O brahmin, those serpents that bite men are different — the dundubhas merely bear the smell of snakes; you ought not to harm them.

sanskrit: ekānarthān pṛthagarthān ekaduḥkhān pṛthaksukhān ḍuṇḍubhān dharmavid bhūtvā na tvaṃ hiṃsitum arhasi
english: Sharing the same calamities but with separate purposes, sharing the same sorrows but with separate joys — you who know dharma ought not to harm the dundubhas."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca iti śrutvā vacas tasya bhujagasya rurus tadā nāvadhīd bhayasaṃvigna ṛṣiṃ matvātha ḍuṇḍubham
english: The Sūta said: Having heard the serpent's words, Ruru then did not kill it, startled and apprehensive, taking the dundubha for a rishi.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ bhagavān ruruḥ saṃśamayann iva kāmayā bhujaga brūhi ko 'sīmāṃ vikriyāṃ gataḥ
english: Then the blessed Ruru spoke to it as if to pacify it gently: "O serpent, tell me — who are you, come to this changed form?"

sanskrit: ḍuṇḍubha uvāca ahaṃ purā ruro nāmnā ṛṣir āsaṃ sahasrapāt so 'haṃ śāpena viprasya bhujagatvam upāgataḥ
english: The dundubha said: "I was formerly a rishi named Sahasrapat, O Ruru; and by the curse of a brahmin I have attained the state of a serpent."

sanskrit: rurur uvāca kimarthaṃ śaptavān kruddho dvijas tvāṃ bhujagottama kiyantaṃ caiva kālaṃ te vapur etad bhaviṣyati
english: Ruru said: "Why did the angry brahmin curse you, O best of serpents? And for how long will you bear this form?"

sanskrit: ḍuṇḍubha uvāca sakhā babhūva me pūrvaṃ khagamo nāma vai dvijaḥ bhṛśaṃ saṃśitavāk tāta tapobalasamanvitaḥ
english: The dundubha said: "I had a friend in former times, a brahmin named Khagama, O dear one, of very sharp tongue, endowed with the power of austerity.

sanskrit: sa mayā krīḍatā bālye kṛtvā tārṇam athoragam agnihotre prasaktaḥ san bhīṣitaḥ pramumoha vai
english: While we were playing in childhood, I fashioned a grass snake and, while he was absorbed in his agnihotra rite, I frightened him so that he fainted.

sanskrit: labdhvā ca sa punaḥ saṃjñāṃ mām uvāca tapodhanaḥ nirdahann iva kopena satyavāk saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Regaining his senses, that one rich in austerity spoke to me, as if burning with rage, he of true speech and firm vows:

sanskrit: yathāvīryas tvayā sarpaḥ kṛto 'yaṃ madbibhīṣayā tathāvīryo bhujaṃgas tvaṃ mama kopād bhaviṣyasi
english: "Just as you made this snake — however powerless — to frighten me, so by my wrath shall you become a powerless serpent."

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ tapaso vīryaṃ jānamānas tapodhana bhṛśam udvignahṛdayas tam avocaṃ vanaukasam
english: Knowing the power of his austerity, O one rich in austerity, with heart greatly distressed, I spoke to that forest-dweller:

sanskrit: prayataḥ saṃbhramāc caiva prāñjaliḥ praṇataḥ sthitaḥ sakheti hasatedaṃ te narmārthaṃ vai kṛtaṃ mayā
english: "Purified in body, trembling, with joined palms, standing bowed low — O friend, this was done by me only for a joke, in jest.

sanskrit: kṣantum arhasi me brahmañ śāpo 'yaṃ vinivartyatām so 'tha mām abravīd dṛṣṭvā bhṛśam udvignacetasam
english: "O brahmin, you must forgive me — let this curse be revoked." But he, seeing my heart greatly distressed, spoke to me:

sanskrit: muhur uṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya susaṃbhrāntas tapodhanaḥ nānṛtaṃ vai mayā proktaṃ bhavitedaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Sighing hotly again and again, greatly agitated, that one rich in austerity said: "What I have spoken cannot be untrue — this will come to pass, somehow.

sanskrit: yat tu vakṣyāmi te vākyaṃ śṛṇu tan me dhṛtavrata śrutvā ca hṛdi te vākyam idam astu tapodhana
english: "But the words I shall now speak to you — hear them, O man of firm vows; and having heard, let these words abide in your heart, O one rich in austerity.

sanskrit: utpatsyati rurur nāma pramater ātmajaḥ śuciḥ taṃ dṛṣṭvā śāpamokṣas te bhavitā nacirād iva
english: "There will be born a pure son of Pramati named Ruru; upon seeing him your release from the curse will come before long."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ rurur iti khyātaḥ pramater ātmajaḥ śuciḥ svarūpaṃ pratilabhyāham adya vakṣyāmi te hitam
english: "You are that one known as Ruru, the pure son of Pramati. Now I shall recover my own form, and I will speak what is beneficial for you.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ smṛtaḥ tasmāt prāṇabhṛtaḥ sarvān na hiṃsyād brāhmaṇaḥ kva cit
english: Non-violence is declared the highest dharma for all living beings; therefore a brahmin must never harm any living creature anywhere.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ saumya eveha jāyateti parā śrutiḥ vedavedāṅgavit tāta sarvabhūtābhayapradaḥ
english: The supreme scripture declares, 'The brahmin is born here as the gentle one' — knowing the Vedas and their auxiliaries, dear one, he grants fearlessness to all beings.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ kṣamā ceti viniścitam brāhmaṇasya paro dharmo vedānāṃ dharaṇād api
english: Non-violence, truthful speech, and forbearance — these are determined to be the supreme dharma of the brahmin, even above the preservation of the Vedas.

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya tu yo dharmaḥ sa neheṣyati vai tava daṇḍadhāraṇam ugratvaṃ prajānāṃ paripālanam
english: But the dharma of the kshatriya does not apply to you here — the bearing of the rod, fierce valor, and the protection of subjects.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ kṣatriyasyāsīt karma vai śṛṇu me ruro janamejayasya dharmātman sarpāṇāṃ hiṃsanaṃ purā
english: That was a kshatriya's deed — hear from me, O Ruru, O righteous soul: the slaying of serpents long ago at Janamejaya's snake sacrifice.

sanskrit: paritrāṇaṃ ca bhītānāṃ sarpāṇāṃ brāhmaṇād api tapovīryabalopetād vedavedāṅgapāragāt āstīkād dvijamukhyād vai sarpasatre dvijottama
english: And the deliverance of the terrified serpents at that snake sacrifice — by a brahmin endowed with the power of austerity and strength, master of the Vedas and their auxiliaries: Āstīka, foremost of twice-born men, O best of brahmins."

sanskrit: rurur uvāca kathaṃ hiṃsitavān sarpān kṣatriyo janamejayaḥ sarpā vā hiṃsitās tāta kimarthaṃ dvijasattama
english: Ruru said: "How did the kshatriya Janamejaya harm the serpents? And why were the serpents harmed, dear one, O best of brahmins?"

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ mokṣitāś caiva pannagās tena śaṃsa me āstīkena tad ācakṣva śrotum icchāmy aśeṣataḥ
english: "And why were the serpents saved by Āstīka? Tell me of him — I wish to hear all of it completely."

sanskrit: ṛṣir uvāca śroṣyasi tvaṃ ruro sarvam āstīkacaritaṃ mahat brāhmaṇānāṃ kathayatām ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: The rishi said: "You will hear, O Ruru, the entire great story of Āstīka from the brahmins who will recount it" — and having said this, he vanished.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ruruś cāpi vanaṃ sarvaṃ paryadhāvat samantataḥ tam ṛṣiṃ draṣṭum anvicchan saṃśrānto nyapatad bhuvi
english: The Sūta said: Ruru also ran through the entire forest in all directions seeking to see that rishi, then exhausted, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: labdhasaṃjño ruruś cāyāt tac cācakhyau pitus tadā pitā cāsya tad ākhyānaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sarvaṃ nyavedayat
english: Ruru regained his senses and came back; he reported all this to his father then, and when asked, his father recounted the entire story.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca kimarthaṃ rājaśārdūlaḥ sa rājā janamejayaḥ sarpasatreṇa sarpāṇāṃ gato 'ntaṃ tad vadasva me
english: Śaunaka said: "For what reason did that tiger among kings, King Janamejaya, bring the serpents to their end with the snake sacrifice? Tell me of that.

sanskrit: āstīkaś ca dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ kimarthaṃ japatāṃ varaḥ mokṣayām āsa bhujagān dīptāt tasmād dhutāśanāt
english: "And why did Āstīka, best of twice-born men, foremost among those who recite prayers, rescue the serpents from that blazing sacrificial fire?"
